note: The comparison covers the two American carriers and three Japanese carriers participating in the Coral Sea carrier battle within the event’s 4–8 May 1942 interval. Shoho served a separate covering force and sank on 7 May; the two Japanese fleet carriers fought on 8 May. This is not a simultaneous two-versus-three surface gunfight or a comparison of equal-sized ships. Lexington and Shoho sank or were scuttled; the separately recorded damage to Yorktown and Shokaku is not added to those sinking counts. Zuikaku’s depleted air group does not make its hull a sinking loss. Original national participants are retained as explicitly unquantified other naval formations, excluding the named carriers. Separate unquantified air components acknowledge the central aircraft attacks without converting aircraft to ships or inventing a common-time aviation strength or loss total. The propeller-aircraft silhouette represents a typical component, not every aircraft type, sortie or air group. No human deaths are inferred. The new carrier model is a straight-deck family analogy; island placement, exhaust and exact hulls vary among the named ships, and the deck is deliberately empty rather than implying a complement. Source event coordinates remain broad locators, not the tactical positions or tracks of these dispersed forces. Formations and animation timing remain illustrative.
